questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a painless ulcer on the right hand with a black eschar and surrounding oedema after handling animal hides. Gram stain of the exudate shows large gram-positive bacilli in chains. What is the drug of choice?
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax caused by Bacillus anthracis is best treated with Penicillin G (IV) or amoxicillin for mild cases. Ciprofloxacin and doxycycline are alternatives for bioterrorism-related or penicillin-allergic cases.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with annular, scaly plaques on the trunk with central clearing and elevated active border. KOH mount shows hyphae. The organism responsible most commonly belongs to which genus?
questions.exp: Tinea corporis (ringworm) is most commonly caused by Trichophyton rubrum. The clinical presentation of annular plaques with central clearing and active scaly margins is classic. KOH shows septate hyphae.

questions.q: A neonate develops grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the scalp and face within 48 hours of birth. Mother had a primary HSV-2 infection near term. Which investigation is most specific for diagnosis?
questions.exp: PCR for HSV DNA from vesicle fluid or CSF is the most sensitive and specific test for neonatal herpes. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells but cannot distinguish HSV type. Viral culture, though gold standard historically, is less sensitive than PCR.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man from an endemic area presents with hypopigmented macules on the trunk. Skin smear from the macule shows no bacilli. Slit skin smear BI = 0, sensation is diminished over the macule. As per Ridley-Jopling classification, this patient has:
questions.exp: Borderline tuberculoid (BT) leprosy presents with few hypopigmented macules with impaired sensation. Slit skin smear is typically negative (paucibacillary). Unlike TT, nerve damage can be more extensive in BT, and lesions may be less well-defined.

questions.q: A 22-year-old sexually active male presents with multiple painful genital ulcers with undermined edges and a soft base. Regional lymphadenopathy is present. Gram stain shows gram-negative coccobacilli in a 'school of fish' pattern. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi and presents with painful soft genital ulcers with ragged undermined edges. The school-of-fish or railroad-track pattern on Gram stain is characteristic. Treatment is azithromycin or ceftriaxone.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with malar rash, discoid lesions, photosensitivity, and oral ulcers. ANA is positive with a homogeneous pattern. Anti-dsDNA antibodies are strongly positive. Which of the following is associated with disease activity in SLE?
questions.exp: Anti-dsDNA antibodies correlate with disease activity in SLE, particularly lupus nephritis. Anti-Sm is specific for SLE but does not correlate with activity. Anti-histone is associated with drug-induced lupus. Anti-Ro is linked to neonatal lupus and subacute cutaneous LE.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman develops tense blisters on normal and erythematous skin. Nikolsky sign is negative. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone. The target antigen is most likely:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) shows linear IgG and C3 at BMZ on DIF. The major antigens are BP180 (type XVII collagen, BPAG2) and BP230 (BPAG1). Desmoglein 1 and 3 are targets in pemphigus. Type VII collagen is the target in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man with a long history of actinic keratoses presents with a rapidly growing, well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma on the lower lip. Which feature indicates the worst prognosis?
questions.exp: Perineural invasion is an independent poor prognostic factor in SCC, associated with higher rates of local recurrence and regional metastasis. Other high-risk features include tumor diameter >2 cm, depth >2 mm, poor differentiation, and immunosuppression.

questions.q: During Mohs micrographic surgery for a basal cell carcinoma on the nose, frozen sections are prepared. What is the unique advantage of Mohs surgery over wide local excision?
opts: Lower recurrence rate due to chemotherapy
Complete microscopic margin assessment (100% margin examination)
Better cosmetic outcome due to skin grafting
questions.exp: Mohs surgery examines 100% of the surgical margin by sectioning horizontally (en face) rather than vertically (bread-loaf). This allows mapping and re-excision of positive margins while sparing maximum normal tissue, resulting in the highest cure rates.

questions.q: A patient with moderate plaque psoriasis does not respond to topical therapy. Methotrexate is initiated. Which baseline investigation is most important before starting methotrexate?
questions.exp: Before starting methotrexate, baseline LFTs, CBC, renal function, and chest X-ray are essential. Methotrexate is hepatotoxic, myelosuppressive, and nephrotoxic. LFTs and CBC are most critical as hepatotoxicity and bone marrow suppression are the most common serious adverse effects.

questions.q: A skin biopsy from a patient with lichen planus shows a saw-tooth pattern of rete ridges, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermo-epidermal junction, and Civatte bodies. What do Civatte bodies represent?
questions.exp: Civatte bodies (colloid bodies or hyaline bodies) in lichen planus represent dyskeratotic keratinocytes undergoing apoptosis at the DEJ. They are eosinophilic, homogeneous, and may contain nuclear remnants. They result from basal cell damage by CD8+ T cells.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with well-defined, silvery-scaled plaques on the elbows and scalp. The Auspitz sign is positive. Biopsy shows parakeratosis, Munro microabscesses, and elongated rete ridges. The pathological hallmark is:
questions.exp: Psoriasis is characterized by epidermal hyperplasia (acanthosis), parakeratosis (nuclei retained in stratum corneum), and loss of granular layer. Munro microabscesses contain neutrophils in the stratum corneum. Spongiform pustules of Kogoj are seen in the spinous layer.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child develops crusted, honey-colored lesions around the nose and mouth after a cold. Culture grows group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus. Which complication is unique to streptococcal (not staphylococcal) impetigo?
questions.exp: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN) can follow streptococcal skin infections (nephritogenic strains). It does NOT occur with staphylococcal impetigo. Scarlet fever, TSS, and SSSS are associated with staphylococcal or other streptococcal systemic toxins.

questions.q: A patient on long-term corticosteroids develops white patches on the oral mucosa that can be scraped off, leaving a bleeding surface. KOH shows pseudohyphae and budding yeast. What is the first-line topical treatment?
questions.exp: Oral candidiasis (thrush) is treated first-line with nystatin oral suspension (swish and swallow). For more severe or refractory cases, systemic fluconazole is used. Nystatin is not absorbed and acts locally, making it safe with minimal systemic effects.

questions.q: A 45-year-old HIV-positive patient develops painless, violet-colored papules and nodules on the lower extremities and oral mucosa. Biopsy shows spindle cells, extravasated red cells, and slit-like vascular spaces. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Kaposi sarcoma is caused by Human Herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8/KSHV). It is an AIDS-defining illness. Histology shows spindle cell proliferation with slit-like vascular spaces and extravasated RBCs. Treatment includes antiretroviral therapy, intralesional vinblastine, or liposomal doxorubicin for systemic disease.

questions.q: A 35-year-old with multibacillary leprosy on MDT develops sudden onset of erythematous, tender nodules all over the body with fever, joint pains, and iritis. Slit skin smear BI = 4+. What is this reaction?
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) is a Type 2 lepra reaction occurring in BL and LL leprosy. It presents with tender evanescent nodules, fever, and systemic features. It is immune-complex mediated. Treatment is thalidomide (or prednisolone). It differs from Type 1 (reversal) which shows upgrading and is cell-mediated.

questions.q: A 24-year-old presents with painless genital ulcer with indurated, clean base and non-tender bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy shows motile spirochetes. The VDRL is reactive. What is the stage?
questions.exp: Primary syphilis presents with the classic painless chancre (indurated, clean-based ulcer) at the site of inoculation with regional lymphadenopathy. VDRL may be reactive or non-reactive at this stage. Dark-field microscopy of the chancre exudate is positive for Treponema pallidum.

questions.q: A 42-year-old woman presents with Raynaud phenomenon, skin tightening involving the fingers and extending to the forearm (but not past the elbows), and telangiectasias. ANA is positive with anticentromere pattern. This is consistent with:
questions.exp: Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc, formerly CREST syndrome) is characterized by skin involvement limited to the distal extremities (distal to elbows/knees) and face. Anticentromere antibodies are highly specific. Diffuse SSc has more proximal skin involvement and anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I).

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with flaccid blisters on the trunk. The blisters rupture easily, leaving raw erosions. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF shows intercellular IgG and C3 in a 'fishnet' pattern. The target antigen is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris shows intercellular IgG (fishnet pattern) on DIF. The antigen is desmoglein 3 (mucosal dominant) and desmoglein 1 (skin involvement). Dsg3 alone causes mucosal disease; Dsg3+Dsg1 causes mucocutaneous disease. Nikolsky sign is positive due to acantholysis.

questions.q: An 8-year-old child presents with a pigmented lesion in the nail matrix extending to involve the proximal nail fold (Hutchinson sign). The most important differential diagnosis to rule out is:
questions.exp: Hutchinson's sign (periungual pigmentation extending to the nail fold) is a worrisome finding suggesting subungual melanoma until proven otherwise. While it can occur in benign conditions (pseudo-Hutchinson's), in adults especially, biopsy is warranted. It is a high-risk feature requiring urgent evaluation.

questions.q: During a patch test for contact allergy, readings are taken at D2 and D4. The patch test shows ++ reaction (vesicles limited to test area, not coalescing). This indicates:
questions.exp: ICDRG patch test grading: + (erythema, infiltration, possible papules), ++ (erythema, infiltration, papules, vesicles), +++ (bullous reaction). A ++ reading indicates strong positive allergic contact sensitization. Irritant reactions show burning, pustules, or papules without infiltration and are graded differently (IR).

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman on isotretinoin for severe cystic acne wishes to become pregnant. What is the minimum recommended duration to wait after stopping isotretinoin before conceiving?
questions.exp: Isotretinoin has a short half-life (10-20 hours for the drug; ~90 hours for 4-oxo-isotretinoin). International guidelines recommend waiting at least 1 month after stopping isotretinoin before conception. However, many practitioners advise 1-3 months. The FDA iPLEDGE program mandates 1 month. The drug is Category X (teratogenic).

questions.q: Langerhans cells are antigen-presenting cells in the epidermis. Which of the following is the characteristic ultrastructural marker of Langerhans cells?
questions.exp: Birbeck granules (also called Langerhans cell granules) are racket-shaped or rod-shaped cytoplasmic organelles unique to Langerhans cells, visible on electron microscopy. They are involved in antigen processing. CD1a and langerin (CD207) are surface markers. Odland bodies are found in keratinocytes.

questions.q: A 16-year-old presents with worsening acne vulgaris with comedones, papules, and a few nodules on the face and back. Which topical agent addresses both follicular hyperkeratinization and bacterial colonization?
questions.exp: Adapalene (retinoid) normalizes follicular keratinization and reduces comedone formation, while benzoyl peroxide is bactericidal against C. acnes and reduces resistance. The combination addresses both pathogenic factors. Monotherapy with retinoids or antibiotics is less effective than combination treatment for mixed acne.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child develops a rapidly spreading vesiculobullous rash with positive Nikolsky sign after a staphylococcal skin infection. The child appears ill with fever. Exfoliative erythroderma develops. Which toxin is responsible?
opts: Exfoliative toxins A and B (ET-A, ET-B)
questions.exp: Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome (SSSS) is caused by exfoliative toxins A and B (serine proteases) produced by S. aureus phage group II. These toxins cleave desmoglein 1 in the superficial epidermis (stratum granulosum), causing bullae and exfoliation. TSST-1 causes toxic shock syndrome.

questions.q: A 20-year-old student from Northeast India presents with hypopigmented patches on the trunk that do not tan. Wood's lamp examination shows the lesions fluoresce golden-yellow. KOH mount shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (and related species). The classic KOH finding is 'spaghetti and meatballs' (hyphae and spores). Wood's lamp shows golden-yellow fluorescence. Lesions are hypopigmented due to azelaic acid inhibiting melanin synthesis. Treatment: topical antifungals or oral fluconazole/itraconazole.

questions.q: A 35-year-old presents with a dermatomal vesicular eruption on the right thorax preceded by 3 days of pain. Treatment with antiviral reduces duration and severity. Post-herpetic neuralgia develops in 20% of cases. What is the antiviral of choice for herpes zoster in immunocompetent adults?
opts: Acyclovir 800 mg five times daily for 7 days
Valacyclovir 1000 mg three times daily for 7 days
Famciclovir 500 mg three times daily for 7 days
Acyclovir 400 mg five times daily for 5 days
questions.exp: Valacyclovir 1000 mg TID x 7 days is the preferred oral antiviral for herpes zoster in immunocompetent adults due to superior bioavailability (3-5x that of acyclovir). Famciclovir 500 mg TID x 7 days is an equivalent alternative. Acyclovir 800 mg 5x/day x 7-10 days is acceptable but requires more frequent dosing.

questions.q: In lepromatous leprosy (LL), skin smears show high bacterial load. The nerve damage in LL is characterized by:
opts: Symmetrical, gradually progressive nerve damage with 'glove and stocking' pattern
questions.exp: In LL leprosy, nerve damage is symmetrical and slowly progressive ('glove and stocking' sensory loss), contrasting with TT/BT where it is asymmetric and affects identifiable nerve trunks. This is because LL involves widespread bacillemia and nerve infiltration diffusely, not focal granulomas compressing specific nerves.

questions.q: A 28-year-old pregnant woman at 36 weeks presents with intensely itchy urticarial papules and plaques on the abdomen starting within striae gravidarum. The periumbilical area is spared. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: PUPPP (Pruritic Urticarial Papules and Plaques of Pregnancy), also called polymorphic eruption of pregnancy, is the most common dermatosis of pregnancy. It begins in abdominal striae, spares the periumbilical area (unlike pemphigoid gestationis), occurs in the third trimester, and resolves postpartum. DIF is negative. Benign prognosis for mother and fetus.

questions.q: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis develops tender erythematous nodules on the anterior leg with histology showing septal panniculitis without vasculitis (Miescher's radial granulomas). No causative infection or drug is found. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum (EN) is the most common form of panniculitis, showing septal panniculitis on biopsy. Miescher's radial granulomas around the septa are characteristic. EN is a reactive condition associated with infections (streptococcus, TB, fungi), sarcoidosis, IBD, drugs (OCP, sulfonamides), and autoimmune diseases.

questions.q: A 60-year-old farmer presents with a warty, verrucous plaque on the dorsum of the foot present for 10 years. Biopsy shows pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, intraepidermal abscesses with copper-coloured muriform cells (sclerotic bodies). The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis (chromomycosis) is caused by dematiaceous (melanin-containing) fungi like Fonsecaea pedrosoi. The pathognomonic finding is sclerotic bodies (Medlar bodies or muriform cells) — copper/brown thick-walled, septate, planate-dividing cells — seen on histology. Treatment: itraconazole long-term, with terbinafine as alternative.
